title: Unauthenticated /api/device?h=Int.max overflows the match arithmetic and aborts the engine process
evidence_before: Reproduced: `swift test --filter DeviceResolutionTests` with the new regression test aborted the test process -- `error: Process '...swiftpm-testing-helper ...' exited with unexpected signal code 5` (SIGTRAP, Swift arithmetic overflow), because GET /api/device passes an unbounded `h` into abs(lhs.height - height) * 1000 + ... Full log: AUDIT/evidence-audit-0001-before.log. APIServer.swift:218-222 reads w and h with no upper bound; DeviceProfiles.swift:241-245 did the arithmetic unbounded.
fix_summary: DeviceProfiles.nearest now bounds width and height (width > 0, height >= 0, both <= the new public maximumViewportDimension = 100_000) before any arithmetic, so no Int can reach the subtractions; a value outside the bound is reported as 'unlike anything known' (nil) instead of trapping. Commit on audit/2026-09-18.
evidence_after: `swift test --filter DeviceResolutionTests`: 7 tests in 1 suite passed, EXIT=0, including 'An absurd viewport is admitted as unknown rather than trapping the process' (Int.max/Int.min width and height). Log: AUDIT/evidence-audit-0001-after.log. Full-suite result recorded under the batch run (see AUDIT/baseline.md gate). AUDIT gate: `bash tools/mac-checks.sh` -> all 8 gates passed, EXIT=0; 1052 tests in 195 suites (baseline 1048), 0 warnings, coverage 52.28% lines (baseline 52.12%), swiftlint 215 (baseline 215), swift-format 439 (baseline 439). title: The only production caller discards ConversationStore.save's failure, so a lost save is silent
evidence_before: Static proof: ConversationEngine+Transcript.swift:79 was `_ = store.save(record)`, the only production call to a @discardableResult method whose false return means disk-full, permission failure or an undecodable index. title: Image pixel-count cap is bypassed for PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, which pass through and are decoded later
evidence_before: DocumentImport.wireRepresentation returns early when AttachedDocument.mediaType(of: data) != nil (line 240), before validateImage() and its maximumImagePixels guard (line 222). The comment at Attachments.swift:299-301 claims those images are never decoded, but TurnLoop.swift:401 (CIImage(data:)) and MLXEngine.swift:344-345 decode exactly those bytes. A sub-64 MB PNG declaring 100000x100000 (or GIF 65535x65535) is accepted and decoded.

title: No aggregate attachment byte bound: 24 x 64 MB are retained and base64-amplified every turn
evidence_before: defaultMaximumFileBytes = 64 MB (Attachments.swift:310) and maximumAttachments = 24 (EngineServiceAttachments.swift:30) are the only bounds; no total-bytes cap exists. ConversationEngine+TurnLoop.swift:169 re-sends attachments to the engine every turn and OpenAIResponsesEngine.swift:230-231 base64-encodes every image into a data URL. Up to ~1.5 GB of uploads, copied several times, on an 8 GB Mac.

title: Transcript interpolates topic and speaker name without stripping newlines, allowing forged entries
evidence_before: TranscriptWriter writes "Topic: \(topic)\n" (line 69) and "[timestamp] \(turn.speakerName.uppercased())\n" (line 85) with no control-character sanitation. EngineService.swift:153-161 accepts any non-blank topic, and seat names are trimmed with .whitespaces (which excludes newline). A LAN client can POST a topic containing a newline plus a fabricated "[timestamp] OTTO" line; Save Conversation then exports a transcript containing the forged entry.
fix_summary: TranscriptWriter flattens CR/LF to spaces and drops other control characters in the topic, participant display names, model short names and the per-turn label, so a newline cannot forge a `[timestamp] NAME` line. The message body is untouched; `indent` already marks its continuations.
evidence_after: New test 'A topic or a speaker name cannot forge a transcript entry' asserts the forged line is absent and exactly one entry line survives. Evidence: AUDIT/evidence-batch3-tests.log -- `swift test --filter 'GenerationCapTests|TranscriptWriterTests|StoreRecoveryTests|BuiltInKeyTests|ConversationStoreTests|EngineStateContextWindowTests'` -> 48 tests in 6 suites passed, EXIT=0.

title: readTemporary reports an unreadable temporary as an empty history and isUnreadable never inspects it
evidence_before: readTemporary() returns [] when the .tmp exists but readIndex() fails, while readAll()'s contract says nil means "exists but cannot be decoded"; save() (line 148) then treats it as empty and overwrites the only copy. isUnreadable (line 277) only checks indexURL, so in exactly the crash state readTemporary exists for it reports false.

title: .secrets.env is read with no permission check and nothing creates it 0600
evidence_before: BuiltInKeys reads .secrets.env with String(contentsOf:) and no mode inspection (OpenAICompatibility.swift:167-171). grep finds no chmod for it anywhere in the repo, unlike CertificateStore.swift:306/320/326 which applies 0o600 to the TLS key. A key file created under the usual umask is 0644 and read silently.
fix_summary: BuiltInKeys.secretsFile restricts a group/world-readable .secrets.env to 0600 on read (restrictToThisUser, the rule CertificateStore applies to the TLS key) and reports the repair or the failure to stderr; the key is still read, so a repaired file does not become 'no key configured'.

title: Tavily URLSession follows redirects while carrying the API key; no redirect-refusing delegate
evidence_before: TavilyClient builds `URLSession(configuration:)` with no delegate (line 78) and sends `Authorization: Bearer \(apiKey)` (line 234). OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:20-26 installs a NoRedirects delegate with the comment that following a redirect is how a validated URL reaches a host that never was; TavilyClient has no equivalent, so a 302 from api.tavily.com is followed with the key attached.

title: Searches are charged only when a turn produces non-empty text, so tool-only turns spend for free
evidence_before: The only call to conversation.research?.record(searchCount:addedSomething:) sits inside the else branch of `if clean.isEmpty` (ConversationEngine+TurnLoop.swift:248-249, 277-278). A turn whose rounds emit only tool calls ends with empty text (Engine/TurnLoop.swift:213-218), so searches and rounds stay 0 and budgetRemaining never drops; the maxSearches ceiling can be bypassed up to configuration.maxTurns (default 40).

title: No per-turn cap on tool calls: 3 rounds x N calls can overshoot maxSearches arbitrarily
evidence_before: maxToolRounds = 3 (TurnLoop.swift:138) caps rounds, and each round dispatches the whole collected list (`for call in toolCalls`, lines 245-250). The search ceiling is checked once before the turn (ConversationEngine+TurnLoop.swift:190-195), so one turn with many <tool_call> blocks spends many billed Tavily calls.

title: fetch_page forwards any http(s) host, including loopback/private/link-local, to the extractor
evidence_before: readableURL accepts any http(s) URL with a non-empty host and no deny-list or resolution check (WebTools.swift:96-105); WebToolValidationTests.swift:30-31 blesses loopback. FetchPageTool delegates the fetch to Tavily (TavilyClient.extract), so a model or injected content can send Tavily to internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or http://2130706433/ and the content returns to the model. Contrast OpenAIModels.swift:101-111, which refuses link-local hosts for model endpoints.

title: Fetched web content enters the prompt undelimited and uninspected for instruction smuggling
evidence_before: WebSearchTool concatenates hit.title/url/content and FetchPageTool returns "Content of \(page.url) (\(page.title)):\n\n\(page.content)" with no fence or untrusted marker; TurnLoop.swift:309 inserts the string verbatim as a role:"tool" entry. A fetched page can therefore inject instructions into the running model, which is allowed to invoke further privileged tools. Newlines in a hostile page title also forge transcript lines in the synthesis prompt (ConversationEngine+Research.swift:44-47, ConversationEngine+TurnLoop.swift:311).

title: synthesisPrompt interpolates the API-settable topic and display names raw, including the transcript boundary token
evidence_before: "The question was: \(question)" and "The analysts were: \(participants.joined(separator: ", "))" (ResearchReporting.swift:113-114) take conversation.topic and seat displayName (ConversationEngine+Research.swift:50-54) with no neutralisation, unlike fencedTranscript() a few lines later. Both are settable through the unauthenticated API, so a topic or seat name can forge the "===== BEGIN SESSION TRANSCRIPT" boundary and inject instructions ahead of the real fence.

title: Conversation history is created with the process umask (0755 dir / 0644 file) rather than private modes
evidence_before: ConversationStore creates its directory (line 136) and writes conversations.json (line 189) with default permissions. Every kept conversation (topic and full transcript, possibly including cloud-seat content) is therefore world-readable on a multi-user Mac, unlike the TLS key which CertificateStore creates 0600.
fix_summary: ConversationStore creates its history directory 0700 and writes conversations.json 0600, so a kept transcript is private rather than the umask's 0755/0644.
evidence_after: New test 'A kept conversation and its directory are owner-only' asserts no group/world bits on either. Evidence: AUDIT/evidence-batch3-tests.log -- `swift test --filter 'GenerationCapTests|TranscriptWriterTests|StoreRecoveryTests|BuiltInKeyTests|ConversationStoreTests|EngineStateContextWindowTests'` -> 48 tests in 6 suites passed, EXIT=0.

title: The whole /api surface is unauthenticated and, through Caddy, reachable from the LAN by design
evidence_before: crossOriginRefusal (APIServer.swift:77-101) blocks cross-origin browser requests and requires application/json, but there is no authentication or authorization anywhere on the routes: any client that can reach the port can read every conversation, drive every control and upload attachments. SECURITY.md documents this as deliberate (the LAN phone use case) and AGENTS.md repeats it; Caddyfile carries no host so it listens on every interface. This is recorded so the risk is explicit rather than hidden, not as an unnoticed defect.

title: Vision support is decided by substring match on short markers (o3/o4) and the test for it is tautological
evidence_before: declaresVision uses visionModelMarkers.contains { name.contains($0) } (VisionSupport.swift:74,82) with markers including "o3" and "o4", so any id containing those substrings is declared vision-capable. VisionCapabilityTests.swift:65 asserts `== .unknown || == .supported`, which passes for .supported and cannot detect the failure it is named for.

title: DeviceClass.desktop resolution is dead: `all` holds no desktop profile so desktop viewports return nil
evidence_before: all = phones + samsung + tablets + androidTablets (line 203) contains only .phone and .tablet entries, but nearest() selects candidateClass .desktop for width >= 1000 or a non-mobile window (lines 230-233) and then filters all by it, so the candidate set is empty and it returns nil (lines 234-235). DeviceProfileTests.swift:121,128 accept nil and cannot detect it.

title: The Tavily key can be passed on the command line, exposing it in argv and shell history
evidence_before: --key stores the value (CommandLine.swift:116) and CLI.swift:52-53 does setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", key, 1). Any local process can read argv and the shell records it in history; TAVILY_API_KEY and .secrets.env are the safe alternatives and are already supported.

title: readBounded swallows a read error with try? and returns a silently truncated file as complete
evidence_before: `guard let chunk = try? handle.read(upToCount: 64 * 1024), !chunk.isEmpty else { break }` (lines 111-114): a mid-file I/O error yields nil, the loop breaks and the partial bytes are returned as the whole document; the caller only reports the extractor's own truncation flag.

title: Unchecked 0..<document.pageCount on an untrusted PDF would trap on a negative count
evidence_before: `for index in 0..<document.pageCount` (line 66) with document built straight from caller bytes (lines 61-63) and pageCount unclamped; a negative value traps on the Range precondition. Whether PDFKit can return a negative count is unconfirmed, hence suspected.

title: TextutilExtractor ignores the bounded data and re-opens url.path, so its size checks cover a different read
evidence_before: The extractor runs /usr/bin/textutil on url.path (lines 143-150) and never uses the `data: Data` parameter, so DocumentIngestor's lstat/regular-file and bounded-read checks (DocumentIngestor.swift:63-68,77) apply to a different read. Exploitability is low (0700 UUID staging dir on the upload path) and SystemProcess's output ceiling still bounds the result.

title: includeAnswer is decoded then discarded; the retry comment claims the answer is preserved
evidence_before: Response declares `let answer: String?` (line 108) but nothing reads it; search returns [SearchHit] only, and the .retryAdvanced branch re-calls with includeAnswer under a comment asserting the answer is no longer dropped. includeAnswer: true remains a no-op.

title: The basic-to-advanced retry makes two billed Tavily calls while the budget charges one
evidence_before: outcome(for:depth:) returns .retryAdvanced for an empty basic result and search recurses at .advanced (lines 138-140), so one web_search tool call costs two billed calls against a budget that charges one (ConversationEngine+TurnLoop.swift:234).

title: Untrusted Tavily response is decoded and mapped with no byte or item-count bound
evidence_before: JSONDecoder().decode(Result.self, from: data) (line 254) has no body cap; search maps every result and extract clips only raw_content, leaving title/url and the array itself unbounded. A hostile or compromised upstream can force large allocations before any limit applies.

title: Vision capability test asserts an outcome it claims to forbid
evidence_before: #expect(spec.visionSupport == .unknown || spec.visionSupport == .supported) is named "A plain checkpoint id is not mistaken for a vision model by substring" but passes when the value is .supported, and its comment claims "qwen3-vl" is a substring of "Qwen3.5-4B", which it is not. The test can only fail if declaresVision returns false.

title: SwiftLint and swift-format are enforced against recorded waiver counts, not --strict, and force_unwrapping is never enabled
evidence_before: mac-checks.sh runs `swiftlint lint --quiet` and `swift-format lint` and compares the finding count to a waiver (217/444) in tools/analysis-waivers.txt; .swiftlint.yml has no opt_in_rules, so force_unwrapping is not on. The brief requires both tools run with --strict so linter warnings fail the build. Baseline: swiftlint 215 findings, swift-format 439 diagnostics.

title: Python has no committed Ruff configuration, so B/E722/S101/PT and datetime/encoding rules are not enabled
evidence_before: No configuration file existed, so `ruff check tools/` ran only E4/E7/E9/F: B, S101, PT, DTZ and unspecified-encoding were not selected (AUDIT/baseline.md records 'clean (default rule set only)'). `ruff check --select B,S101,PT,DTZ,PLW1514,E722 tools/` measured 1 finding, plus 5 unspecified-encoding findings once the preview rule was enabled.
fix_summary: Added a committed ruff.toml selecting E4/E7/E9/F/B/S101/PT/DTZ/PLW1514 with lint.preview so the bare-except, mutable-default, assert-validation, pytest-style, naive-datetime and unspecified-encoding rules are all in force, then fixed all six findings it raised (B007 in embed-web.py; PLW1514 in embed-web.py, embed-names.py and hf-file-list.py) plus the same unencoded-IO class in capture_setup.py and capture_render.py that the rule does not reach. target-version is py313, not 3.14, so the formatter does not emit PEP 758 except-without-parentheses syntax that CI's older python3 cannot parse.
evidence_after: `ruff check tools/` -> All checks passed. `ruff format --check tools/` -> 10 files already formatted. `python3 -m py_compile tools/*.py` clean, `pyright tools/` 0 errors, `python3 tools/embed-web.py --check` and `tools/embed-names.py --check` still in sync. Rule proof in AUDIT/tool-coverage.md (AUDIT/probes/python-rules-probe.py: B006, S101, DTZ005, PLW1514, PT011 all fire). AUDIT gate: `bash tools/mac-checks.sh` -> all 8 gates passed, EXIT=0; 1052 tests in 195 suites (baseline 1048), 0 warnings, coverage 52.28% lines (baseline 52.12%), swiftlint 215 (baseline 215), swift-format 439 (baseline 439). Log: AUDIT/evidence-batch1-mac-checks.log.
commit: audit(AUDIT-0030): the Python rules the brief names are configured and green

title: JavaScript has no committed formatter or linter and no pinned toolchain
evidence_before: web/ holds 11 browser-facing JS modules on the LAN-served page and there is no package.json, no eslint/prettier config and no npm dependency scanner. The only JS checks are the two hand-written behavioural rules in tools/check-web-deltas.js and tools/check-web-votes.js; nothing checks syntax, escaping or unused bindings across the other nine modules.

title: The client cannot observe the peer certificate, so the documented 'mismatch is visible' claim is false
evidence_before: WebTransportClient.swift:15-16 says the fingerprint is reported and logged 'so a mismatch is visible even though it is not enforced', but the client uses trustPolicy .localDevelopmentSelfSigned, whose library path sets tls.peerAuthentication(.none); WebTransportNetworkSession exposes no peer-certificate accessor. TransportCheck.swift:130-132 reports the local file's fingerprint while claiming it is 'the one on the other end of the socket', and Checks.swift:37 loads a local identity that is never used. An operator who reads the note believes an impersonating loopback peer is detectable; by construction it is not.

title: A reconnecting client cancels but never awaits the old reader, which can poison the new session's shared state
evidence_before: teardown() only calls readerTask?.cancel() and clears the single client-wide readerError/pendingReplies/eventContinuation, without awaiting the task. The reader checks cancellation only at the top of its outer loop (WebTransportClientReader.swift:28), so a chunk already returned by receive() is fully processed. connect() then installs a new readerTask/eventContinuation (:196-208). The old reader waking later calls failReader, which finishes the new greeting's continuation and sets the shared readerError, so the new connect fails with the old error (send at :333-335). Triggered by the reconnect path at :150-152.

title: Two paths close a session twice, contradicting the code's own 'exactly one closer' invariant
evidence_before: refuseFraming does `try? await session.close(reason:)` and serve's defer then closes the still-owned entry again; the startup watchdog (:42) closes and the defer closes again. WebTransportServer.swift:201-203 states the library's close() must not be called twice. The library's lease release is idempotent so the practical impact looks nil, but the documented invariant is false.

title: A session that cannot open its stream ends with no recorded reason
evidence_before: `guard let stream = try? await session.acceptBidirectionalStream() else { return }` discards the error and records no note(), unlike every neighbouring refusal path (:85, :138, :144, :161). recentSessionErrors/lastSessionError stay empty for this failure, indistinguishable from a clean close.

title: The TLS key is world-readable under a permissive umask until a post-hoc chmod, and the run directory is never restricted
evidence_before: openssl writes -keyout privateKey.path under the process umask and restrictToThisUser(privateKey) chmods afterwards (:374); the code concedes this at :310-315. Under umask 022 the key exists 0644 in the window. The run directory is created with default mode and never verified (tools/start-app.sh:71 is a plain mkdir -p), and permissions(of:) at :328-331 follows symlinks.

title: stop() closes every session serially on the MainActor with the library's 15 s per-session timeout
evidence_before: `for session in liveSessions { try? await session.close() }` runs serially; the configuration never sets timeoutMilliseconds, so each close uses the library default 15000 ms, and up to 16 unresponsive peers can block the main actor for minutes during shutdown. The library's bounded shutdown(gracePeriodMilliseconds:) is not used.

title: Per-session receive buffer can be driven to the ~85 MB protocol cap with no aggregate budget
evidence_before: LengthFraming.read only rejects a declared length above ProtocolLimits.maximumMessageBytes (~85 MB); buffer.append(chunk) accumulates per session (line 89) and once one whole frame arrives the session joins spokenSessions (line 110), disarming the startup watchdog. 16 sessions x 85 MB is about 1.3 GB on an 8 GB machine, from a loopback peer.

title: The installer's green banner reports a canned session count and waits with a fixed sleep instead of a readiness signal
evidence_before: report.sessionCount = 1 is hardcoded (line 321) rather than read from the server the check started, and `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(400))` (line 317) is the only wait for the event stream. succeeded does not depend on either, so the banner is not evidence of what it claims.

title: SECURITY.md's claim that the TLS key lives in .run/ is false for installed builds
evidence_before: RunDirectory.resolve returns .run only when Package.swift is found; otherwise ~/Library/Application Support/ChatBots. The released app runs from ~/Applications, so its private key lives in Application Support (and in Time Machine copies). CertificateStore.swift:107-108 also says 'Defaults to the project's .run' although directory is a required parameter with no default.

title: Unchecked fcntl(F_SETFL) can defeat the deadline the certificate path relies on
evidence_before: `_ = fcntl(descriptor, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK)` discards the result. If it fails, drain()'s non-blocking assumption is broken, read() blocks, collectOutput's deadline is unreachable, and CertificateStore's openssl invocation can wedge engine start instead of timing out.

title: Two tasks write the same stream; the claimed single serialization point is not enforced by a primitive
evidence_before: The per-session writer task (:63-68) and the initial state send (:77) both call send(), which is documented as the one place that serialises them (:166-168); MainActor isolation is reentrant at await stream.send, so the two can overlap. The library likely serialises whole sends, making this ordering-only, but no primitive in this code enforces it.

title: A checkpoint-declared context window is accepted unvalidated and can overflow the generation cap
evidence_before: contextWindowFor reads max_position_embeddings/max_sequence_length and accepts any positive Int (lines 253-257), which becomes settings.contextWindow. With thinking .unlimited, ChatModels.swift:179 returns answerBudget + max(highHeadroom, contextWindow) and TurnSettings.generationCap adds 4096, so a config.json declaring a value near Int.max traps in TurnSettings.swift:42-45, reached from TurnLoop.swift:100. A model id reaches the hub with no allow-list.
fix_summary: MLXEngine.contextWindow(of:) now clamps a checkpoint-declared window to the new MLXEngine.maximumContextWindow (1_048_576), and ThinkingMode.generationCap clamps its Int addition with addingReportingOverflow, so no config.json value can trap the process.
evidence_after: New test 'A declared context window near Int.max cannot trap the cap arithmetic' passes (Int.max window and Int.max answer budget both clamped, not trapped). Evidence: AUDIT/evidence-batch3-tests.log -- `swift test --filter 'GenerationCapTests|TranscriptWriterTests|StoreRecoveryTests|BuiltInKeyTests|ConversationStoreTests|EngineStateContextWindowTests'` -> 48 tests in 6 suites passed, EXIT=0.

title: unload() cannot cancel an in-flight load; the stale continuation installs the container afterwards
evidence_before: unload() cancels loadingTask and nils it, but the load body's `do { let container = try await task.value; self.container = container; self.loadingTask = nil; onStateChange(.ready) }` still runs if the loader completes despite cancellation. stop() clears generationTask while the load group is parked in engine.load(), so setModel can rebuild and unload the old engine mid-load; the discarded engine keeps a checkpoint resident and posts .ready after being unloaded.

title: sessionReuseProbe drives container.perform without the MLX gate
evidence_before: `let results = try await container.perform { ... }` (line 31) does not acquire MLXGate.shared, whose own doc (MLXGate.swift:8-20) says concurrent Metal evaluation aborts with EXC_BAD_ACCESS and that every Metal-touching operation is serialised through it. Only caller is the single-engine --session-probe, so it is latent.

title: removeAttachment validates a UUID case-insensitively then matches the uppercase string, refusing a lowercase id
evidence_before: `guard UUID(uuidString: id) != nil` accepts a lowercased id, then `engine.attachments.filter { $0.id.uuidString != id }` compares against the uppercase uuidString and removes nothing, so the reply is 'there is no attached file with that id'. castVote (:284-289) parses to UUID and does it correctly.
fix_summary: removeAttachment parses the id once with UUID(uuidString:) and filters by UUID equality, so a lowercased id (which the validity guard already accepted) removes the file instead of reporting it absent.
evidence_after: New test 'The id is matched as a UUID, so a lowercased one still removes the file' passes. Evidence: AUDIT/evidence-batch2-tests.log -- `swift test --filter 'EndpointPolicyTests|AttachmentRemovalTests|TraceSwitchTests|ClientsKeyTests|ResponsesRequestTests|TurnLoopRuleTests'` -> 48 tests in 8 suites passed, EXIT=0 (build clean, warnings-as-errors). title: Link-local refusal is a string prefix and misses IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal forms
evidence_before: endpointRefusal refuses host.hasPrefix("169.254.") || hasPrefix("fe80:") || hasPrefix("[fe80:"). Foundation strips the brackets from an IPv6 literal, so http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/ yields host ::ffff:169.254.169.254 and passes; http://[0:0:0:0:0:ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/ likewise. The [fe80: branch is dead for url.host. The accepted URL then also passes into the streaming client.
fix_summary: endpointRefusal now parses the host to bytes: IPv6 literals via inet_pton (fe80::/10 and the ::ffff:IPv4 mapped range) and IPv4 in dotted-quad, decimal-integer and 0x-hex form, instead of the three string prefixes (one of which, "[fe80:", was dead because url.host has the brackets stripped). Mapped loopback and LAN addresses stay usable.
evidence_after: New test 'A link-local address is refused however it is spelled' pins ::ffff:169.254.169.254, the expanded 0:0:0:0:0:ffff:a9fe:a9fe form, :8080, 2852039166 and 0xA9FEA9FE as refused, and mapped loopback and 192.168.1.10 as allowed. commit: audit(AUDIT-0050/0051/0052/0054/0055/0046/0048): the batch-2 endpoint and engine fixes

title: Malformed SSE data lines are silently skipped, so a truncated answer can be reported as complete
evidence_before: `guard let event = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(payload.utf8)) as? [String: Any] else { continue }` drops an undecodable data: line with no notice; a later well-formed response.completed finishes the turn with whatever text survived, indistinguishable from a complete answer.

title: Changing a seat's baseURL or API key is reported by the snapshot but never reaches the live client
evidence_before: engine.updateSeat(spec) stores the new baseURL/apiKey on the seat but only pushes displayName/persona/thinking to the live engine; ConversationEngine.setEndpoint(_:for:) has no callers, and OpenAIResponsesEngine.spec is a let with a cached client. POST /api/seat (unauthenticated) and the API sheet therefore show an endpoint change that does not take effect until the engine process restarts. This also blocks the obvious remote repoint-then-exfiltrate chain, so it is a facade rather than an active hole.

title: The app adopts any process answering on 7790 without verifying it, then hands it every Keychain API key
evidence_before: start() does `if await isEngineAnswering() { state = .running(owned: false); return }`; the probe uses WebTransportEngineClient with .localDevelopmentSelfSigned, which does not verify the peer. ChatBotsApp.swift:115 then calls controller.applyAPIEndpoints, and APIEndpointStore.swift:53-58 fills apiKey from the Keychain and sends it via .updateSeat. A same-user process that binds 127.0.0.1:7790 receives the user's cloud keys and can inject snapshot.error/notices into the UI. Precondition is local code execution as the user, which is exactly what the Keychain boundary is meant to contain.

title: An engine refusal is treated as acceptance, clearing the moderator draft and showing a refused checkpoint as applied
evidence_before: deliver() does `_ = try await client.send(request); return true`. A .refused reply is a normal reply (only .failed throws), so EngineService.swift:171-173 refusing an over-2000-character steer still returns true; deliverModeratorDraft then clears the box (draft(afterSendOf:accepted:true:)) and discards the reason, and setModel sets pane.spec.modelID for a checkpoint the engine refused. The tests that claim to pin both only cover the no-client case.

title: Cancellation-blind retry loops: try? Task.sleep turns a paced poll into a hot spin after the view disappears
evidence_before: `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(400))` swallows CancellationError and neither loop checks Task.isCancelled, so after the window's .task is cancelled the 400 ms pacing is gone and the loop spins (QUIC connect + state + disconnect) for the full 90 s. terminateChild nils self.process before returning, so the cancelled start() cannot see the killed child and finally assigns state = .failed, overwriting the .idle set by shutdown(). ChatControllerConnection.swift:37 has the same shape and can install a client after cancellation. The poll loop at ChatControllerConnection.swift:73-76 does check Task.isCancelled.

title: Attachments are read fully into memory on the main thread with no size cap
evidence_before: addFiles is @MainActor and does `queued.append((name, try Data(contentsOf: url)))` synchronously, contradicting the doc comment that says the upload runs in the background. There is no size or count check, while the engine caps at 64 MB per file and 24 files, so several large PDFs/TIFFs block the UI and buffer everything before the Task starts.

title: The launch path falls back to a world-writable fixed path and inherits the app's whole environment
evidence_before: candidates.append(URL(fileURLWithPath: "/usr/local/bin/chatbots-cli")) and `candidates.first { isExecutableFile(atPath:) }` with no signature check anywhere in Sources; process.environment is never set, so the child inherits OPENAI_API_KEY/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY/TAVILY_API_KEY/CHATBOTS_TRACE_API, and then receives every seat API key over the wire. Arguments are built only from a UInt16 port, so there is no argument injection.

title: start() guards only .running, so a concurrent start can launch a second engine on the same port
evidence_before: `if case .running = state { return }` does not guard .starting, and launch() ends with self.process = process (line 245), overwriting any earlier child. A second start() while the first is still in its cancellation-blind 90 s loop can start a rival engine; the file's own comment (lines 266-271) records that failure mode.

title: terminateChild early-returns on a nil process, leaking the log file handle after a failed launch
evidence_before: launch() opens and assigns logHandle (lines 238-242) before process.run() (line 244). If run() throws, self.process stays nil, terminateChild's `guard let process else { return }` returns before the `try? logHandle?.close(); logHandle = nil` at lines 163-164, so one descriptor leaks per failed launch.

title: The whole never-rotated engine log is read into memory on the MainActor
evidence_before: tailOfLog does `try? String(contentsOf: logURL, encoding: .utf8)` on the full file. The log is opened append-only and nothing rotates or truncates app-engine.log; it is created 0644 under ~/Library/Application Support/ChatBots and, with CHATBOTS_TRACE_API set, also carries conversation content.

title: Closing the window shuts the engine down but never disconnects the controller; the poll task survives
evidence_before: `onDisappear { Task { await supervisor.shutdown() } }` and nothing calls controller.disconnect(). The QUIC session and the 1 s poll task stay alive against the killed engine; the loop only exits when client.readerError is set, so a connection that merely times out keeps a 1 s failing poll, each send up to 10 s, for the life of the app process.

title: The persisted text scale is trusted on read; a corrupted preference traps in Int(...)
evidence_before: `@AppStorage("textScale") private var storedScale: Double = TextZoom.default` with `get { storedScale }` and a clamping setter. TextZoom.percent is `Int((scale * 100).rounded())`, which traps for NaN or a value outside Int's range, and minimumWindowSize feeds the raw scale into NSSize. The app never writes an out-of-range value itself, so the trigger is a corrupted preference.

title: Keychain write failures are swallowed and deleteKey has no caller
evidence_before: setKey calls `Self.storeKey(value, seat: seat)` and discards the @discardableResult Bool from SecItemAdd; storeKey first deletes the old item (line 171), so a failed add silently destroys the previous key while the sheet still shows the new one as configured. static func deleteKey(seat:) (line 179) is never called.

title: HTTP connection slots can be held indefinitely: the idle deadline is re-armed by any chunk (slowloris)
evidence_before: The idle deadline is re-armed on every received chunk (`if chunk != nil { self.armIdleDeadline(for: connection) }`) and there is no total-request deadline, so a client that declares a large Content-Length and then sends one byte every <30 s holds its slot forever. maximumConnections defaults to 32 (HTTPServer.swift:153) and accept answers 503 once reached, so 32 tricklers can permanently refuse the whole website/API from the LAN. Caddy forwards the body progressively and the shipped Caddyfile sets no upstream timeout.

title: SSE has no backpressure and no idle deadline, so a non-reading client buffers every token without bound
evidence_before: `connection.send(content: Data(frame.utf8), completion: .contentProcessed { _ in })` has no flow control and no backlog/failure signal; the API broadcasts one frame per token/reasoning fragment/tool event, and a streaming connection's idle deadline is disarmed (HTTPServer+Connections.swift:103) so a silent stream is never reaped. GET is exempt from crossOriginRefusal (APIServer.swift:78), so any LAN client can open /api/events, stop reading, and let Network.framework accumulate frames for the life of the process.

title: The same-origin check compares Origin against Host/X-Forwarded-Host, so DNS rebinding defeats it
evidence_before: `originHost == addressedHost` compares two names the browser derives from the URL it fetched. A page served at http://evil.example:7788 that DNS-rebinds to the Mac sends Origin evil.example and X-Forwarded-Host evil.example (Caddy sets it from the original Host; the Caddyfile carries no host so any Host is served), so a same-origin POST is accepted and Sec-Fetch-Site is same-origin. Chrome Private Network Access may block public-to-private fetches; Safari and Firefox do not implement it.

title: 403, 415 and 431 are written with the reason phrase OK
evidence_before: `reason` has no case for 403, 415 or 431, so `default: "OK"` produces `HTTP/1.1 403 OK`, `415 OK` and `431 OK` for exactly the statuses the HTTP layer's own guards return (callers APIServer.swift:88,93,98).

title: /api/seat silently ignores an unrecognised thinking or backend value and answers 200
evidence_before: `thinking: body.thinking.flatMap(ThinkingMode.init(rawValue:))` and `backend: body.backend.flatMap(AgentSpec.Backend.init(rawValue:))` turn an unknown value into nil, which EngineService reads as 'leave it', so the route returns the unchanged state with 200. Sibling routes 400 an unknown value via unknownValue (lines 104-106, 139-142), the policy MalformedBodyTests pins.

title: /api/seat applies every other field before the model change can refuse, so a 409 still changed state
evidence_before: `engine.updateSeat(spec)` runs at line 213; only afterwards can the modelID branch return .refused("the model cannot be changed while a turn is in flight"). POST /api/seat {"seat":"a","name":"X","modelID":""} during a run answers 409 while the seat is already renamed, against the method's own rule that a change that could not be made is never reported as one that was.

title: A bare CR or LF inside a header value is accepted
evidence_before: The head is split only on CRLF (`components(separatedBy: "\r\n")`) and `.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)` does not strip CR/LF, so `X-A: v\nY: b` yields one field whose value contains a bare LF with no control-character check. No sink was found: no response header reflects a request header value, and Caddy sanitises CR/LF when re-serialising upstream headers. Recorded as parser leniency.

title: The event feed's seen set retains one UUID per turn for the life of the process
evidence_before: `var seen = Set<UUID>()` sits outside `for await turns in self.engine.transcriptUpdates`, and `for turn in turns where !seen.contains(turn.id) { seen.insert(turn.id) ... }` accumulates every turn ever produced (across newConversation) until process exit. Low impact.

title: The shipped default publishes the unauthenticated site and API on every interface over plaintext HTTP
evidence_before: Caddyfile:40 `http://:7788 {` carries no bind, so the site listens on every interface; bind 127.0.0.1 is only generated when --local-only is passed (start.sh:53 defaults LOCAL_ONLY=0). /api/* and /s/* proxy to loopback with no authentication or TLS, so anyone on the LAN can read and steer conversations and an on-path reader can also write. SECURITY.md documents the exposure as deliberate and start.sh prints it; recorded as a sign-off item because the shipped default is the exposed one.

title: --gates-log satisfies the release gate by grepping a caller-supplied file for the gate's own success string
evidence_before: `[ -f "$GATES_LOG" ] || die` and `grep -q 'Mac-only gates passed' "$GATES_LOG" || die` are the only checks; nothing binds the log to $HEAD_SHA, to this machine, or to a real tools/mac-checks.sh run, although the comment at :173 claims 'on this same commit'. Any file containing that literal is accepted, so the release gate can be satisfied by text rather than by a passing run.

title: A bundle that cannot be code-signed, or does not verify, still exits 0 and is packaged for release
evidence_before: make-app.sh prints `! the app could not be signed` / `! the app is signed but does not verify` but ends with `echo "Built: $APP"` and success status; install.sh:150 and make-release.sh:193-202 treat that as success, and the release log scan for `error: ` does not match either warning line. No signature check exists anywhere in make-release.sh.

title: $MODEL_DIR is unbound under set -u, so the installer's failure diagnostics are replaced by a shell error
evidence_before: The heredoc opened at install-verify.sh:118 prints `· a partial model download — delete $MODEL_DIR and run this script again`, but MODEL_DIR is only a `local` inside install_checkpoint (install-models.sh:212). Reproduced on /bin/bash 3.2: the heredoc fails with `MODEL_DIR: unbound variable` (status 127), the guidance block never prints, and install.sh continues to `ChatBots is installed.` and exit 0. MODELS_DIR is the variable that exists.

title: An empty DEFAULTS array aborts the start-web wrappers on macOS's bash 3.2
evidence_before: `exec bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/start.sh" "${DEFAULTS[@]}" "$@"` with `DEFAULTS=()` and `set -u`: with both defaults suppressed, `${DEFAULTS[@]}` is an unbound-variable error on bash 3.2. Reproduced: `bash tools/start-web-desktop.sh --view phone --open none` prints `DEFAULTS[@]: unbound variable` and exits 127, so start.sh never runs. tools/fetch-metal.sh:203 uses the `${...[@]:-}` workaround.

title: Model weights are verified by byte length only, and the expected length comes from the same origin that serves the bytes
evidence_before: The expected size is fetched from huggingface.co itself (`curl -fsIL ... | awk '/content-length:/'`), and the only comparison is `actual = expected` byte length. hf-file-list.py reads only rfilename, discarding any per-file metadata. A same-length substituted payload, or a `main` revision that moved between the size snapshot and the download, is recorded as a complete checkpoint; HTTPS is the only compensating control.

title: rm -rf runs on a caller-supplied --scratch path with no sanity check
evidence_before: `--scratch) SCRATCH="${2:?--scratch needs a directory}"` accepts any path and :191 runs `rm -rf "$SCRATCH" "$STAGING"`. `--scratch "$ROOT"` or `--scratch .` deletes the checkout after the clean-tree check at :112, and `--scratch /` is passed through to rm -rf. The default is safe; no prefix check (e.g. must be under $ROOT/.build) exists.

title: The swift-format gate discards the tool's exit status and can pass with zero diagnostics when the tool fails
evidence_before: `find ... | xargs -0 swift-format lint > "$logs/swift-format.txt" 2>&1` never examines the pipeline status, then `diagnostics=$(grep -cE 'warning:|error:' ... || true)`. A swift-format that runs but fails without emitting such a line (or xargs invoked with no operands) yields 0 diagnostics and PASSes inside the recorded waiver. Mechanisms visible in code; not reproduced.

title: Generated artifacts are read and written without an explicit encoding, so they depend on the ambient locale
evidence_before: `(WEB / filename).read_text()`, `TARGET.write_text(wanted)`, `open(sys.argv[1])`, and `config.write_text(...)` use locale.getencoding(). A non-UTF-8 locale can mis-decode web/ or names/ (whose bytes are compiled into the shipped binary) or write different bytes than `--check` expects. third-party-notices.py and semgrep-waivers.py pass encoding="utf-8", so the omission is inconsistent within the same directory.

title: The model directory name derived from a user-supplied repo id is not validated, unlike hub-supplied names
evidence_before: `local MODEL_DIR_NAME="${MODEL_ID##*/}"` / `local MODEL_DIR="$MODELS_DIR/$MODEL_DIR_NAME"`; resolve_checkpoint passes any argument containing / through verbatim, so `--model 'x/..'` yields MODEL_DIR_NAME=".." and downloads would be written into the checkout root. model-target-path.sh:32-37 refuses `..` and absolute names for hub-supplied files only. The config.json check makes a usable exploit unlikely; the finding is the asymmetric validation.

title: A websocket frame length from the peer is unbounded, though the recorded waiver says the reply is read with a bound
evidence_before: `length = struct.unpack(">Q", self._read_exactly(8))[0]` then `payload = self._read_exactly(length)` with no cap (only the HTTP target list is bounded via MAX_TARGET_LIST_BYTES). The waiver in tools/analysis-waivers.txt justifies the insecure-websocket finding by saying "the reply is read with a bound", which overstates the control. The peer is loopback Chrome with a host/port check, so impact is same-user only.

title: Follow is never turned off in the split desktop layout, so streaming yanks every pane to the bottom
evidence_before: wire() (app.js:333) runs before apply(), and the scroll listener loop over containers() only ever sees #thread, because containers() enumerates document.querySelectorAll(".transcript") and the pane transcripts are created later by buildPanes (app-transcript.js:113-123); index.html's pane-template content is not in the document. state.follow is written nowhere else (initialised true at app-core.js:34) and in split layout #thread is hidden, so every redraw calls scrollToBottom(), including on every streaming delta. A reader cannot scroll back while a reply streams.

title: A typed topic is committed only on change and is not ordered before Start, so it can be silently dropped
evidence_before: $("topic").addEventListener("change", ...) posts /api/topic, while $("start").onclick posts /api/start and the Cmd/Ctrl+Enter shortcut clicks start; the two POSTs are neither awaited nor sequenced. If start is handled first, the topic is refused (EngineService.swift:162-164, setTopic guard ConversationEngine.swift:316) and the room runs the previous topic while the user sees an error. Pressing Start with the field still focused may never fire change at all.

title: One Cmd/Ctrl+Enter in the message box both sends the message and presses Start, resetting the conversation
evidence_before: The message keydown handler calls send() and preventDefault() but not stopPropagation(), so the window handler then also matches Enter and clicks #start. start → /api/start → startOrRestart → reset() when startedTurns > 0 (ConversationEngine.swift:323-330, +Lifecycle.swift:141-157), clearing turns, queued steering, votes and report. Both handlers are on the bubble path of the same keystroke.

title: The Enter that commits a rename re-enters startRename and leaves a second handler pair that re-posts the rename
evidence_before: The button's keydown handler is not disabled while contentEditable is true and calls startRename(button), which adds onBlur/onKey to the same button; on Enter both run in registration order, so the pane handler re-enters startRename and each Enter accumulates another pair that later posts /api/seat again for an already-committed name.

title: --session-probe sends its follow-up questions with role .assistant
evidence_before: `role: turn == 1 ? .user : .assistant` selects the role from the turn number while the content on turns 2 and 3 is a question, so the prompt becomes system, user(Q1), assistant(Q2/Q3), which is not the shared-prefix session the probe claims to measure.

title: --memory-probe reports a failed turn as if it ran and still exits 0
evidence_before: `for turn in 1...3 { _ = try? await engines[...].generate(...); report("after turn \(turn)") }` swallows the error, unlike the session probe which exits 1 on a failed generate (lines 50-55) and on a failed load (22, 96-102). A model that loads but fails to generate yields a plausible memory table for turns that produced no tokens.

title: Flags only --serve or --benchmark can honour are accepted and silently ignored
evidence_before: --port (195-204) and --share-base (205-215) are used only in ServeCommand; --solo (254) only in Benchmark. The parser deliberately refuses the same class elsewhere: --seed without --serve exits 2 (CLI.swift:21-27) and --transport without --serve exits 2 (CommandLine.swift:265-272). `chatbots-cli --port 9999 --turns 2` never binds anything and exits 0. Also `--attach` with no value appends an empty path (line 172).

title: The default headless run always exits 0, even when every turn failed
evidence_before: The function ends with header("END"), a 'done' log and a notices loop, with no check of engine.status/lastError and no non-zero exit path — the false-success class the sibling modes were fixed for (Benchmark.swift:15-19; Probes.swift:18-22,50-55). No repo script consumes this exit code, so impact today is limited to a caller that discards stderr.

title: .gitignore's unanchored models/ also matched Sources/ChatBotsCore/Models/, so new source files there were silently ignored
evidence_before: `git check-ignore -v Sources/ChatBotsCore/Models/.audit-ignore-probe` returned `.gitignore:8:models/` on this case-insensitive filesystem (`core.ignorecase=true`), while the existing tracked files were unaffected — so a new file added to the Models source directory would be silently skipped by `git add`, and it surfaced here only when adding a modified tracked file under that path was refused.
fix_summary: Anchored the three checkpoint patterns to the repository root: `/models/`, `/models/.huggingface-file-list.txt`, `/models/.hf-model.json`, with a comment saying why. The root models/ directory is still ignored; Sources/ChatBotsCore/Models/ is no longer matched.
evidence_after: A new file under Sources/ChatBotsCore/Models/ is no longer ignored (check-ignore prints nothing), and a new file under the root models/ still matches `/models/`.
